verses.zh: 來 啊 ， 我 們 要 向 耶 和 華 歌 唱 ， 向 拯 救 我 們 的 磐 石 歡 呼 ！
verses.en: Come, let us sing for joy to the Lord.Let us shout out praises to our Protector who delivers us.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 95. The psalmist summons Israel to praise God as the creator of the world and the nation’s protector, but he also reminds the people not to rebel against God.

verses.zh: 我 們 要 來 感 謝 他 ， 用 詩 歌 向 他 歡 呼 ！
verses.en: Let us enter his presence[NOTE:1] with thanksgiving.Let us shout out to him in celebration.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to the rocky summit of our deliverance.”

verses.zh: 因 耶 和 華 為 大 神 ， 為 大 王 ， 超 乎 萬 神 之 上 。
verses.en: For the Lord is a great God,a great king who is superior to[NOTE:1] all gods.

verses.zh: 地 的 深 處 在 他 手 中 ； 山 的 高 峰 也 屬 他 。
verses.en: The depths of the earth are in his hand,[NOTE:1] and the mountain peaks belong to him.

verses.zh: 海 洋 屬 他 ， 是 他 造 的 ； 旱 地 也 是 他 手 造 成 的 。
verses.en: The sea is his, for he made it.His hands formed the dry land.

verses.zh: 來 啊 ， 我 們 要 屈 身 敬 拜 ， 在 造 我 們 的 耶 和 華 面 前 跪 下 。
verses.en: Come, let us bow down and worship.[NOTE:1] Let us kneel before the Lord, our Creator.
notes: The phrase “in his hand” means within the sphere of his authority.

verses.zh: 因 為 他 是 我 們 的 神 ； 我 們 是 他 草 場 的 羊 ， 是 他 手 下 的 民 。 惟 願 你 們 今 天 聽 他 的 話 ：
verses.en: For he is our God;we are the people of his pasture,the sheep he owns.[NOTE:1] Today, if only you would obey him.[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 你 們 不 可 硬 著 心 ， 像 當 日 在 米 利 巴 ， 就 是 在 曠 野 的 瑪 撒 。
verses.en: He says,[NOTE:1] “Do not be stubborn like they were at Meribah,[NOTE:2] like they were that day at Massah[NOTE:3] in the wilderness,[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “if only you would listen to his voice.” The Hebrew particle אִם (ʾim, “if”) and following prefixed verbal form here express a wish (cf. Ps 81:8). Note that the apodosis (the “then” clause of the conditional sentence) is suppressed.
The words “he says” are supplied in the translation to clarify that the following words are spoken by the Lord (see vv. 9-11).

The name Meribah means “strife.” Two separate but similar incidents at Meribah are recorded in the Pentateuch (Exod 17:1-7; Num 20:1-13, see also Pss 81:7; 106:32). In both cases the Israelites complained about lack of water and the Lord miraculously provided for them.

The name Massah means “testing.” This was another name (along with Meribah) given to the place where Israel complained following the Red Sea Crossing (see Exod 17:1-7, as well as Deut 6:16; 9:22; 33:8).

verses.zh: 那 時 ， 你 們 的 祖 宗 試 我 探 我 ， 並 且 觀 看 我 的 作 為 。
verses.en: where your ancestors challenged my authority[NOTE:1] and tried my patience, even though they had seen my work.
notes: Heb “do not harden your heart[s] as [at] Meribah, as [in] the day of Massah in the wilderness.”

verses.zh: 四 十 年 之 久 ， 我 厭 煩 那 世 代 ， 說 ： 這 是 心 裡 迷 糊 的 百 姓 ， 竟 不 曉 得 我 的 作 為 ！
verses.en: For 40 years I was continually disgusted[NOTE:1] with that generation,and I said, ‘These people desire to go astray;[NOTE:2] they do not obey my commands.’[NOTE:3]
notes: The prefixed verbal form is either a preterite or an imperfect. If the latter, it emphasizes the ongoing nature of the condition in the past. The translation reflects this interpretation of the verbal form.
Heb “a people, wanderers of heart [are] they.”

verses.zh: 所 以 ， 我 在 怒 中 起 誓 ， 說 ： 他 們 斷 不 可 進 入 我 的 安 息 ！
verses.en: So I made a vow in my anger,‘They will never enter into the resting place I had set aside for them.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they do not know my ways.” In this context the Lord’s “ways” are his commands, viewed as a pathway from which his people, likened to wayward sheep (see v. 7), wander.
